transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (CTO, Northshore), Marta Lopez (Dir ML Ops), Evan Chen (Infra), Jules Park (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick model catalog walkthrough, deep-dive on benchmarks and quantization/compatibility matrix, questions about VPC/private deployment for PHI. Action items recorded.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. I'm Alex Rivera, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me is Priya Singh, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Sam (CTO): Good, thanks. Ready to see how this model catalog thing looks — we've been evaluating open models for summarization and triage tasks.
[00:13] Priya (SE): Great. Quick agenda: I'll do a short demo of the model catalog and the Console, show benchmark examples and the compatibility matrix for quantization/GPU types, and then we'll talk about deployment options — hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC). Leave time for Q&A at the end.
[00:28] Marta (ML Ops): Sounds good. Our main constraints: PHI handling, latency SLOs around 250ms p95 for short prompts, and total cost targets. We want to avoid big accuracy regressions if we quantize.
[00:38] Alex (AE): Perfect — we'll call those out as we go. Priya, kickoff the catalog?
[00:42] Priya (SE): Yep. (screen share) So here's the Redwood model catalog. You can filter by task — summarization, chat, embeddings — and by model family. We have curated open models and then Redwood-verified performance profiles. For each model you get inference throughput, latency med/p95, token cost estimate, and a quality score derived from our eval sets.
[01:05] Priya (SE): For Northshore specifically, based on the prompt set you mentioned in the form, I'd point to two families: the Llama-3 variants (we host quantized 8-bit and 4-bit profiles) and a few instruction-tuned Pythia/Redwood-finetuned mix. Here's an example compatibility matrix — shows which GPUs (A100, H100, RTX) and quant levels (fp16, int8q, int4) are supported and any known issues with KV cache or long-context.
[01:34] Evan (Infra): Quick clarifying question — that compatibility matrix, is it per model version? We have some older models in prod with custom tokenization.
[01:41] Priya (SE): Yes it's per model-version. In the Console you can pin a specific model version and see exact kernel/quantization compatibility. Tokenization differences are noted; we also keep sample tokenizer outputs.
[01:51] Sam (CTO): Can you show an example benchmark for a short prompt, like a triage note gen? We're trying to understand p95 and cost tradeoffs if we move from fp16 to int8q.
[02:02] Priya (SE): Sure — here's a benchmark we ran on a 2048 prompt distribution (link: drive.re/redwood/benchmarks/northshore-sample). This is a Llama-3-13B variant. fp16 on A100 gives p95 ~210ms and cost X tokens/unit. int8q on same hardware drops cost ~40% but p95 goes to ~260ms and we saw a small drop in ROUGE/F1 on the medical summarization eval — about 1.8 points.
[02:29] Marta (ML Ops): That aligns with our fear. 1.8 points could be meaningful for clinical triage. How deterministic are those quality deltas?
[02:36] Priya (SE): They vary by prompt set. For some instruction-style prompts the delta is <1 point; for domain-specific wording it can be larger. We recommend targeted evals on your exact prompt set as a gating criteria, and Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles based on those evals.
[02:52] Alex (AE): And to add — we can run a short pilot where we benchmark your prompt set across model variants and quantization levels; that helps make the cost/accuracy trade explicit.
[03:02] Jules (Product): What about streaming vs non-streaming? Many of our UI flows need partial results under 200ms.
[03:08] Priya (SE): Streaming can reduce perceived latency — we have streaming endpoints in the Redwood API and the Console shows token-level timing. But streaming is only helpful if the first token can be generated quickly; large decoder overheads still exist. We have examples in the Console showing token emission timing.
[03:24] Sam (CTO): On the security side — we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. Also VPC peering or Private deployment because some PHI can't leave our VPC.
[03:38] Alex (AE): Absolutely. Redwood Private is designed for that — the control plane can be customer-hosted or we can do a VPC-private deployment. We support KMS/HSM integrations, and our security pack includes SOC 2 artifacts and standard audit log formats. Priya will share the security docs.
[03:53] Priya (SE): One note: Private deployments have slightly different ops model; latency can be better since you control networking, but there's an onboarding window. For Dedicated — reserved pools — you get isolation and SLAs but still hosted by Redwood.
[04:07] Marta (ML Ops): For Dedicated, how are versions and rollouts handled? We need canary rollouts and rollback policies.
[04:14] Priya (SE): Redwood Console has rollout controls: canary percent, traffic split by route, automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if SLOs are missed. We also surface per-route latency/cost breakdowns and token-level traces for debugging.
[04:30] Evan (Infra): Regarding networking: we use strict egress rules and need to confirm whether the private control plane will accept connections only from our VPC endpoints.
[04:38] Alex (AE): We'll include a network diagram in the security pack and Priya can follow up to confirm specifics.
[04:45] Priya (SE): Back to the catalog — here's the compatibility matrix in table form. (read aloud) Llama-3-13B: fp16 (A100/H100) supported, int8q supported on A100/H100 with minor kernel fallbacks, int4 experimental on H100 only, KV cache stable up to 8k tokens for fp16, int8q shows some slower cache warmup.
[05:10] Sam (CTO): You mentioned kernel fallbacks — does that increase latency unpredictably?
[05:14] Priya (SE): In some workloads yes: if we need to fall back to a slower kernel for certain ops, you'll see a small increase in tail latency. Our profiler flags those cases and the Console shows recommended configs to avoid fallback paths.
[05:27] Marta (ML Ops): On observability, can we see token-level cost breakdowns per route? We need to map tokens to billing and to product features.
[05:36] Priya (SE): Yes, the Console has per-route token cost breakdown, per-model token counts, and you can export CSVs to feed into your cost dashboards.
[05:45] Jules (Product): For the pilot, what's a reasonable size? We want to test 3 models x 2 quant configs across 1 week of traffic.
[05:53] Alex (AE): That sounds reasonable. We'll propose a 3-week pilot: week 1 lab benchmarks on your prompt set, week 2 shadowed traffic with metrics collection, week 3 controlled canary and cost analysis. Pricing and seat terms we'll include in the follow-up.
[06:08] Sam (CTO): Any other vendors we should be aware of? We're talking to Anthropic and evaluating Vertex for managed endpoints. Also someone's looking at Replicate for self-hosting.
[06:18] Alex (AE): Good to know — we often see similar comparisons. We'll include a short doc comparing model hosting tradeoffs and what Redwood gives you around rollout and caching.
[06:26] Marta (ML Ops): A technical question: how does Redwood handle KV cache across autoscaled pods? If we scale to many workers, do you shard the KV cache or is it per-container?
[06:36] Priya (SE): Good question. Our runtime manages KV cache per model session and we have intelligent routing to reuse warm caches; for large scale we use a combination of per-pod cache + shared prefix caching to reduce re-computation. The Console shows cache hit rates so you can tune batching and affinity.
[06:53] Evan (Infra): And what about GPU choice recommendations — H100 vs A100 — for our 13B and 70B experiments?
[07:00] Priya (SE): For 13B, A100 with int8q often hits the best cost/latency point. For 70B, H100 with optimized kernels is usually required for reasonable latency at scale. We'll include model-specific recommended SKUs in the compatibility matrix.
[07:15] Sam (CTO): If we want Private deployment inside our VPC, how long does onboarding take?
[07:21] Alex (AE): Typical onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and whether you want a customer-hosted control plane. We'll surface a timeline in the POC scoping call.
[07:30] Jules (Product): Can Redwood Optimize generate suggested configs automatically?
[07:33] Priya (SE): Yes — Redwood Optimize analyzes your prompt set and traffic patterns and suggests batching, cache, and quantization profiles. It can also estimate unit costs and simulate rollout regressed quality.
[07:45] Sam (CTO): Excellent. One last question: how reproducible are the bench results across clouds? If we run the same test on GCP vs AWS, do numbers vary much?
[07:55] Priya (SE): They can vary due to kernel versions and instance types; our compatibility matrix has per-cloud notes. For critical comparisons we recommend running a short benchmark in your target region. We'll run that as part of the pilot.
[08:06] Alex (AE): Wrapping up — recap of next steps: we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility matrix, security docs, and a pilot proposal. Priya will follow up on network/security specifics. Marta and team will provide prompts and SLOs.
[08:19] Marta (ML Ops): That works. Expect our prompts by Monday.
[08:22] Sam (CTO): And we'll confirm stakeholders for the POC scoping call.
[08:26] Alex (AE): Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and proposed times.

End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcript with occasional name attribution errors and minor word swaps (e.g., KV cache noted as K V cache). Links referenced: drive.re/redwood/benchmarks/northshore-sample, security.re/redwood/northshore-pack.pdf.
